StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition.issue: RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30, same shape, current lines. The destination-pile DECISION is replaced by an after-the-fact move. The sim has the matching hook -- hooks.modify_card_play_result_pile (hooks.py:604-611) -- and this power does not use it, reaching into the piles from on_card_played instead. Hook order, EXECUTED: combat.py:842 calls `self.hooks.modify_card_play_result_pile(card, "discard")` BEFORE the play-count loop even starts, and `self.hooks.on_card_played(card, is_auto_play)` fires at combat.py:904, inside/after that loop -- so `modify_card_play_result_pile` (Nostalgia's hook) always runs first. NostalgiaPower (powers.py:4132-4141+) uses the hook and, when it applies, moves the card to the top of the draw pile there; ReboundPower then runs its `on_card_played` and finds nothing in `player.discard_pile` (powers.py:3237 `if card not in ... discard_pile: return`), so it silently does neither its move nor its tick. In C# both are listeners on ONE ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition chain (Hook.cs:1391-1405) and the last writer wins, so both always get a say; which one wins in C# is hook_dispatch G2's listener-order question and is not re-verdicted here. OBSERVABLE: with both powers active, a Rebound stack silently survives a play Nostalgia redirected (see the AfterModifyingCardPlayResultPileOrPosition entry) -- Rebound's discard-pile-count/duration is wrong for the rest of the turn, and the played card ends up on the draw-pile top via Nostalgia's placement rather than potentially Rebound's, a placement-order difference a replay comparison would catch. TRIGGER, EXECUTED: both are ordinary registered Ironclad Power cards -- `ReboundCard` (cards/trash_heap_cards.py:245-271, a Trash Heap event reward, `PowerCmd.apply(..., ReboundPower, 1, applier=ctx.player)`) and `NostalgiaCard` (cards/colorless_powers.py:178-199, a normal colorless Power, `PowerCmd.apply(..., NostalgiaPower, 1, applier=ctx.player)`) -- so the contention is reachable on any run that draws and plays both in one combat. FIX: port ReboundPower onto `hooks.modify_card_play_result_pile` (return "draw_top"/equivalent when its own guard passes and it has stacks left) instead of `on_card_played`, so it participates in the same one-decision chain as Nostalgia. RADIUS: this is the sim-side half of `audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json`'s gap G4 (the missing dedicated ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition/AfterModifying two-hook machinery); see the AfterModifyingCardPlayResultPileOrPosition entry.

AfterModifyingCardPlayResultPileOrPositi.issue: RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30, current line 3241 (`self._tick()` inside `on_card_played`, the same method as the previous entry). C# consumes the stack from a DEDICATED after-hook (ReboundPower.cs:32-39 -> PowerCmd.Decrement), which Hook.ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition fires over exactly the listeners that changed the value (Hook.cs:1396-1405). The sim has no such after-hook at all -- confirmed by grep: `hooks.py` defines `modify_card_play_result_pile` (the Before/decision hook) but no `after_modifying_card_play_result_pile_or_position` counterpart exists anywhere in hooks.py or combat.py. So Rebound's stack tick is folded into its own `on_card_played` move: the tick fires if and only if the move fired, which is the right coupling in isolation but the wrong mechanism, and it is exactly what silently drops the tick under the Nostalgia contention in the entry above (when Nostalgia's hook already moved the card, `on_card_played` finds nothing in the discard pile and `self._tick()` at :3241 never runs). TRIGGER: identical to the entry above -- ReboundCard + NostalgiaCard both in play. FIX: not independently fixable from the fix above -- porting Rebound onto the shared `modify_card_play_result_pile` hook and having it self-tick there (mirroring C#'s dedicated after-hook, which fires only over listeners that actually changed the pile) closes both entries together. RADIUS: same absent machinery as `audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json`'s gap G4, one family over; not re-verdicted here per binding rule 3.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the player-side leg moved off the sim's Hook.BeforeTurnEnd slot (`on_player_turn_end`) onto `after_player_turn_end`, which combat.py:809 dispatches AFTER `_process_turn_end_cards` and the hand flush -- the sim's port of Hook.AfterTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1307), the dispatcher for AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292). VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading combat.py:781-812 and this power's class in powers.py. WAS: the effect ran inside Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, so its order relative to the turn-end card effects, the flush and Stampede's turn-end auto-plays was hook registration order. The registration-order witness is doubly gone: StampedePower also moved, to `after_auto_post_play_phase_entered` (powers.py:1089), which combat.py:789 fires strictly before this slot.

guards.rationale: powers.py:2790-2791 tests `card not in player.discard_pile`, which is the sim's way of asking the same question -- power cards leave combat and exhausted cards are already gone, as the sim's comment says. Equivalent for the ported pile set.

powers.py:2793 appends to draw_pile, and the sim's convention is that the list END is the top of the draw pile (stated at powers.py:2793 and used identically by NostalgiaPower). Correct position, not just correct pile.

guards.what: Rebound redirects the Rebound card itself
guards.rationale: The power is applied during Rebound's own resolution, so the card that applied it is the first play redirected -- on both sides. C# gets this from the power being registered before the pile chain runs; the sim's docstring (powers.py:2779-2780) states it and the on_card_played ordering delivers it.
